> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1146e8063100686e910c58b82c35b5da3c209f6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b434c8ff7c8d35181a096dde3370868a7abffa18` — the merge of head `ea824accde20bfd7744f63dce6d8435416f0a228` into base `e1146e8063100686e910c58b82c35b5da3c209f6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b434c8ff7c8d35181a096dde3370868a7abffa18 && git checkout b434c8ff7c8d35181a096dde3370868a7abffa18
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e1146e8063100686e910c58b82c35b5da3c209f6 ea824accde20bfd7744f63dce6d8435416f0a228 && git checkout -B drift-repro e1146e8063100686e910c58b82c35b5da3c209f6 && git merge --no-ff ea824accde20bfd7744f63dce6d8435416f0a228

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1146e8063100686e910c58b82c35b5da3c209f6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e1146e8063100686e910c58b82c35b5da3c209f6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzj7TEH65FDimZdn1H3

**Epic red-line review of #32223 (#32160, uninstall revokes by (package, name), ADR-0150 D8) at head 44f8da18: PASS.** I read the diff against main, but did not run it. Contract review and ACCEPT are seat 4's. The build follows card 1 of the #31698 carriers, including the null-grant stance I ruled.

- **Red line 1, never loosen: holds.**
  - A grant bound to another package is left alone. That package still holds the set, so this grant is not the uninstalled package's to take.
  - A null-column grant is revoked in every case, and is never bound to the remaining holder. Each branch in `cleanupPackagePermissions` revokes or leaves the grant. None writes a package into it.
- **Red line 2, report and never guess: holds.**
  - A null-column grant revoked while another holder still serves the name is reported: one `warn` per uninstall, and `reportedGrants` on the outcome. Both name the user, the organization and the set.
  - When the holder reader cannot answer, every revoked null-column grant is reported. The cleanup never assumes the uninstalled package was the only holder. Pinned.
  - A leftover body still naming the withdrawn package does not count as another holder. Pinned.
- **Red line 3, releasable: holds.**
  - With one holder, the uninstall answer is unchanged, and `reportedGrants` is absent. That is pinned at the unit and the cleanup-runner level.
  - The new member is optional on metadata-protocol TS types, not on spec. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.
  - The defect cannot be reached until #31698 narrows, because install still refuses a second holder.
- **Recorded, not owed:** the holder reader is the served catalog list, so a disabled remaining holder does not trigger a report. That matches my holder-set ruling (#32183). The revocation itself does not depend on the reader.

My review rests on the dev report 6768388605 for the ablation the card asked for: removing the package filter turns the two-holder pin red. The seat's contract review confirms it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `44f8da18d8f340191c3c88e6d28fe7fc78226df6`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **Face.** Declaration. No published schema and no governed path. `UninstallCleanup` and `UninstallCleanupOutcome` are `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` TypeScript types. No `cleanups` shape exists in `packages/spec/src`.
- **Item 1.** `cleanupPackagePermissions` now deletes only the grants of a declared name whose trimmed `permission_set_package` is the uninstalled package or blank. A grant bound to another package is never selected for deletion. The selection runs over the `{ permission_set: name }` read, so with one holder the deleted set equals today's.
- **Item 2.** A blank-column grant is revoked in both cases. It is reported only when its delete landed and the security catalog, read after the withdrawal (`createSecurityCatalogReader(...).list('permission')`), still lists another holder of the name. An environment-authored holder counts as `(environment)`. An unreadable catalog reports the grant with an "unknown" holder, which fails toward reporting and never toward binding. Nothing binds the row to the remaining holder (red line 1).
- **Receipt.** An optional `reportedGrants: { user, organization, permission_set }[]` goes on the cleanup result and the outcome. `runUninstallCleanups` copies it only when it is non-empty, so every answer without a report is byte-identical. It reaches `deletePackage` and install-local's `DELETE`, and it is pinned on both: the runner test and `marketplace-install-local-uninstall-cleanups.test.ts`.
- **Warn.** One `warn` per uninstall names each reported grant's user, organization and set, plus the remedy (re-grant with the package named). It stays apart from the existing refusal `warn` and the `info` line.
- **Pins.** The card's four pins are present, plus the receipt. The two-holder pin asserts the survivor by id: `ups_z_delta` is still present and still bound to `com.qa.delta`. The null-column two-holder pin asserts that the only grant of the name left is `ups_z_delta`, which shows nothing was bound. Ablation, read from report 6768388605 (not re-run here, per the read-only shape): A1 removes the package filter (`|| 'ABLATED-1'`) through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, and 6 tests fail, including 'two holders, each with a bound grant: uninstalling one leaves the other's grant'. The file was restored to blob == HEAD. A2 (report gate), A3 (call-site relay) and A4 (runner relay) are each red as well.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on both the body and the changeset. One optional member is added to an answer, and with one holder nothing changes. Agreed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Authorization boundary.** Not loosened. Today, no grant that this change spares is reachable, because install refuses a second holder until #31698 narrows. Once it is reachable, the spared grant belongs to a package that still holds its set. A grant that names no package is still revoked, never handed to the remaining holder.
- **Epic red-line read.** Owed before landing and requested at this head.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-90rlop`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzi1tLRTEYwYGtbNCyk`

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 卸载一个包时，只撤销绑定到这个包的权限集授权，以及没有写明包的授权。绑定到别的包的授权不再被误删。没写明包、但同名权限集仍有别的包持有的授权，照样撤销，并在一条告警和卸载回执的 `reportedGrants` 里列出用户、组织和权限集名。
- **为什么改：** ADR-0150 允许两个包各自持有同名权限集（#31698 的放宽）。按旧逻辑，卸载 gamma 会连带撤销用户对 delta 同名权限集的授权，而 delta 仍在。所以这张卡要先于 #31698 PR-2 落地。
- **风险与回滚：** 今天安装仍拒绝第二个持有者，所以线上每个卸载回答都和以前一样。回执只多一个可选字段，单持有者时不出现。回滚只需 revert 本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/cleanup-package-permissions.ts` 的授权循环（包过滤和告警），`security-plugin-start-hooks.ts` 的清理注册（持有者读取器和回执），`protocol-class-head.ts` 的 `runUninstallCleanups`（字段转交）。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/cleanup-package-permissions.test.ts`，预期 19 个测试全绿，其中 9 个是本卡新增的 ADR-0150 D8 用例。
- **需要你做的：** 无，席位落地。

席位意见：ACCEPT。契约复核 PASS（comment 6768423371，TIER_DEFAULT，声明面，钉 44f8da18）；其后只有一个散文面提交，记录续管（见下行）。epic 红线 PASS，并在 ea824acc 重申（6768711142）。

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `ea824accde20bfd7744f63dce6d8435416f0a228`

1. **Shape.** 9 files, +479/-26. `Fixes #32160`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on body and changeset. Surface = claim 6766769927 plus amendment 6768437547 (the docs page); the install-local test file sits under the claimed install-local door.
2. **Premises measured.** In the diff: deletion selects `permission_set_package ∈ {this package, blank}` only; blank-column grants are reported after a landed delete when the post-withdrawal catalog still lists another holder (or cannot be read); `reportedGrants` is relayed only when non-empty, so one-holder answers are byte-identical.
3. **Gates (check-runs at ea824acc).** 53: 38 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed; `mergeable_state` clean. K = 3 against PRBASE `e1146e80`; no display label touched.
4. **Prose face, read sentence by sentence.** The `permission-sets.mdx` uninstall sentence now says what the code does: grants bound to the package or to no package are revoked, a grant bound to another holder stays, and an unbound grant of a name another holder keeps is revoked and named under `reportedGrants`. The changeset's three bullets match the code too.
5. **Out of scope, routed.** None. #31698 PR-2 (seat 3) is unblocked on this card once it merges. `Skills-docs: none`.
6. **Landing.** `check-governed-merges --pr 32223` reads 0 of 9 paths governed and 505 lines, so it is Tier S. The seat lands it.
